requirements.requirement: On node1, rotate /var/log/inventory/app.log daily and retain seven compressed rotations.
requirements.summary: The installed rule explicitly sets daily, rotate 7, and compress; logrotate parsed those settings through the global configuration, the daily timer was enabled and active, and a forced rotation produced a valid gzip archive. The rule, timer, active log, and archive remained healthy after restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing to the active log after rotation.
requirements.summary: A writer kept the original file descriptor open across a copytruncate rotation. Its pre-rotation entry appeared in the compressed archive and its subsequent write appeared in the active log, directly demonstrating continued writing.

overall_summary: Both task outcomes are satisfied. The restart protocol is complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged a scheduled reboot, returned with a different boot identity, and recovered the timer, configuration, active log, and compressed archive. Fixed lifecycle observations independently corroborate the boot change and healthy final node state.
limitations: Seven-generation pruning and a naturally elapsed daily rotation were not observed end-to-end; retention and cadence are established by the parsed configuration, active daily scheduler, and one controlled rotation rather than by waiting through multiple daily cycles.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the rotation rule was required; the forced rotation, temporary held-descriptor writer, and resulting test records were bounded behavioral evidence; temporary coordination files were removed. The scheduled reboot served the mandatory restart protocol. Post-executor observations show no failed services, added exposure, package damage, or abandoned temporary files. The changed SSH process IDs and systemd-private paths are normal restart effects.
